info.name: Theana Mansour - Service 1 - Users and Identity Management
info.description:
Service 1 – Users and Identity Management (by Theana Mansour)

Run on a fresh database:

1. create the admin with `python -m services.users.create_admin`
    
2. set admin_login and admin_password in Variables
    
3. send the requests in order (0 to 68).

request.description: Logs in with the administrator set in the collection variables admin_login / admin_password and saves the token.
Anyone can create a Regular Employee account.
The alias Regular User is accepted and stored as Regular Employee.
Only administrators can create privileged roles.
Administrator creates an Auditor.

item.name: 5- Admin registers a user to delete later

request.description: Created by the administrator (so the registration audit record points to the administrator, not to this user) and never logs in. No record points to it, so it can be deleted even when Service 5 keeps its logs in the shared database.

item.name: 6- Register admin role without logging in

request.description: Creating a Security Administrator without logging in is rejected.

exec: pm.test('Message: Username already exists', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Username already exists'); });

request.description: Usernames are unique, ignoring capital letters.

exec: pm.test('Message: Email already exists', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Email already exists'); });

request.description: Emails are unique, ignoring capital letters.
Every field is required.

exec: pm.test('Message: Invalid email format', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Invalid email format'); });

request.description: Email format is validated.
Passwords need at least 8 characters including a letter and a number.
Only the four system roles are accepted.

exec: pm.test('Message: username must be between 3 and 50 characters', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('username must be between 3 and 50 characters'); });

request.description: Usernames must be 3-50 characters.

exec: pm.test('Message: A JSON object is required', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('A JSON object is required'); });

request.description: Malformed requests are rejected.
Input like ' OR '1'='1 is never run as SQL; here it fails email validation.

exec: pm.test('Token is a JWT (3 parts)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().token.split('.').length).to.eql(3); });

request.description: Saves employee_token.

exec: pm.test('Token is a JWT (3 parts)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().token.split('.').length).to.eql(3); });

request.description: Login also works with the email address. Saves analyst_token.

exec: pm.test('Token is a JWT (3 parts)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().token.split('.').length).to.eql(3); });

request.description: Saves auditor_token.
Saves alias_token
Failed authentication.
Same message as a wrong password, so attackers can't tell which usernames exist.
Both fields are required.

exec: pm.test('No password hashes returned', function () { pm.response.json().forEach(function (u) { pm.expect(u).to.not.have.property('password_hash'); }); });

item.name: 43- Employee tries to register an admin

exec:
pm.test('Status code is 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });
pm.test('Message: Only administrators can assign roles', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Only administrators can assign roles'); });

request.description: A logged-in employee still cannot create an Security Administratorc.
Administrator changes a user's role.
The alias is saved as Regular Employee.

item.name: 46- Check the role was saved as Regular Employee

exec: pm.test('Role is Regular Employee', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().role).to.eql('Regular Employee'); });

request.description: Confirms the stored role.

request.description: Only administrators manage roles.
Only the four roles are accepted.

item.name: 49- Admin tries to change own role

exec: pm.test('Message: Cannot change your own role', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Cannot change your own role'); });

request.description: Administrators cannot change their own role.
Returns exactly valid, user_id, username and role.
Suspends the account.
The token was valid a moment ago; it stops working once the account is suspended.

item.name: 53- Suspended user tries to log in

exec: pm.test('Message: Account is not active', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Account is not active'); });

request.description: Suspended accounts cannot log in.
Inactive accounts are also blocked.

item.name: 55- Inactive user tries to log in

request.description: Inactive accounts cannot log in.
Back to Active.
The same token is accepted again.
Only Active, Inactive or Suspended.

item.name: 59- Admin tries to change own status

request.description: Administrators cannot suspend themselves.
Only administrators manage account status.
Malformed tokens are rejected.
Missing token.

exec: pm.test('Message: User deleted successfully', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('User deleted successfully'); });

request.description: Successful deletion of a user with no linked records (no assets, incidents or audit logs point to it).
After deletion the user no longer exists.
